Once a day around 06:00: our people wake rested.  Without it they never slept for real (non-followers aren't allowed to, and the home bed only adds an effect), so their sleep deprivation climbed past vanilla's threshold and 'lets out a huge yawn' / 'tiredly rubs their eyes' flooded the log all day (suffer.cpp without_sleep; variety pass).

Once a night, 23:00-01:00, at the first calm check (it retries every 30 minutes while something hostile is around): our people without a bed at home (bands, visitors, children, babies) lie down where they are and sleep about five hours (the vanilla 'sleep' effect: the tileset draws them asleep, and the Horn wakes them).  The night watcher stays up.  Residents use their beds (household.json).

then.u_message: <global_val:pf_say_a> sits on an upturned bucket, sharpening a knife on a stone, slow and even.
<global_val:pf_say_a> mends a sock with a needle and a lot of muttering.
<global_val:pf_say_a> reads a battered paperback with the cover torn off, moving their lips a little.
<global_val:pf_say_a> writes something in a notebook, then crosses it out, then writes it again.
<global_val:pf_say_a> counts their ammunition, then counts it again.
<global_val:pf_say_a> stands at the edge of the place for a long while, just watching the road.
<global_val:pf_say_a> takes their boots off and stretches their toes in the air with a groan of pure joy.
<global_val:pf_say_a> sorts a pile of scavenged screws by size, for no reason anyone can see.
<global_val:pf_say_a> hums the same four bars of some song over and over, and doesn't seem to know they're doing it.
<global_val:pf_say_a> naps sitting up, chin on their chest, one hand still on their weapon.
<global_val:pf_say_a> sits in a doorway, watching the rain come down, and doesn't say anything for an hour.
<global_val:pf_say_a> sets out every pot and can they own to catch the rain, and looks very pleased with themselves.
<global_val:pf_say_a> curses the rain, the mud, and the rain again.
<global_val:pf_say_a> wrings out their socks for the third time today and gives up on them.
<global_val:pf_say_a> stands under the eaves with their face turned up, letting the rain wash it.
<global_val:pf_say_a> plays a slow game of checkers on a board scratched into the floor, listening to the rain on the roof.
<global_val:pf_say_a> patches a leak with a strip of tarp and a lot of language.
<global_val:pf_say_a> lies in the sun with their eyes closed, like a cat.
<global_val:pf_say_a> hangs washing on a line strung between two posts.  Nothing has ever looked so normal.
<global_val:pf_say_a> spreads damp gear out on the ground to dry, and guards it like treasure.
<global_val:pf_say_a> finds a warm patch of wall and leans on it with their eyes shut.
<global_val:pf_say_a> takes their shirt off to feel the sun, and gets told they're blinding everyone.
<global_val:pf_say_a> wanders off alone and comes back an hour later with nothing to show for it, looking better for it.
<global_val:pf_say_a> checks on everyone in turn, asking how they're holding up, and actually listens to the answers.
<global_val:pf_say_a> goes round checking everyone's socks for holes.  Nobody is spared.
<global_val:pf_say_a> scrapes the last bits out of every empty can and stacks the cans in a neat tower.
<global_val:pf_say_a> adds another tally mark to a board by the door.  Nobody asks what they're counting.
<global_val:pf_say_a> practices with their weapon where everyone can see, and pretends not to notice anyone watching.
<global_val:pf_say_a> writes something in a notebook and snaps it shut whenever anyone comes near.
<global_val:pf_say_a> sharpens a knife a little longer than a knife needs sharpening.
<global_val:pf_say_a> walks the edge of the place twice, then a third time, just to be sure.
<global_val:pf_say_a> brings a cup of something hot to the person they argued with last, and leaves it without a word.
<global_val:pf_say_a> shows <global_val:pf_say_b> a card trick.  <global_val:pf_say_b> pretends not to know how it works.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> argue, at length and with diagrams in the dirt, about whether the dead can swim.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> split a can of peaches, passing the fork back and forth.
<global_val:pf_say_a> cuts <global_val:pf_say_b>'s hair with a pair of kitchen scissors.  It could be worse.  It could also be better.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> talk quietly about before.  Neither of them says what they lost.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> try to fix a radio together, and get a few seconds of static that has everyone gathering round.
<global_val:pf_say_a> teaches <global_val:pf_say_b> a song from where they grew up.  <global_val:pf_say_b> gets the words wrong on purpose.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> play cards for buttons.  <global_val:pf_say_b> cheats, badly, and <global_val:pf_say_a> lets it go.
<global_val:pf_say_a> holds the ladder while <global_val:pf_say_b> fixes something on the roof, and offers advice nobody asked for.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> carry water together, swapping the heavy end without a word.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> try to remember every flavor of ice cream there ever was.  The list gets long.
<global_val:pf_say_a> patches <global_val:pf_say_b>'s jacket.  <global_val:pf_say_b> complains about the color of the thread the whole time.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> plan, in great detail, the garden they will have one day.
<global_val:pf_say_a> reads aloud to <global_val:pf_say_b> from a water-stained magazine, doing all the voices.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> take turns at the grindstone, and talk about nothing at all.
<global_val:pf_say_a> shows <global_val:pf_say_b> how they used to tie a tie.  Neither of them has a tie.
<global_val:pf_say_a> keeps picking up something that belonged to the one they lost, and putting it down again.
<global_val:pf_say_a> sits by themselves for a long while.  Someone leaves food next to them, and later it's gone.
<global_val:pf_say_a> starts to say something to nobody, stops, and goes back to work.
<global_val:pf_say_a> works twice as hard as anyone today, and won't stop when they're told to.
<global_val:pf_say_a> laughs at something, then looks guilty for laughing.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> spend the day carefully not being in the same place.
<global_val:pf_say_a> sits with you, shoulder to shoulder, and for a while neither of you says anything.
<global_val:pf_say_a> saves you the spot by the fire, and pretends they didn't.
<global_val:pf_say_a> leans against you while the others talk, warm and heavy and half asleep.
<global_val:pf_say_a> steals the last bite off your plate, and grins when you notice.
<global_val:pf_say_a> finds your hand in the dark and holds onto it until the fire burns down.
<global_val:pf_say_a> tells you something about themselves they haven't told anyone here, very quietly.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> sit a little apart from the others, talking quietly.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> share one blanket and argue about who's hogging it.
<global_val:pf_say_a> falls asleep against <global_val:pf_say_b>'s shoulder, and <global_val:pf_say_b> doesn't move for an hour.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> laugh at something nobody else heard.
<global_val:pf_say_a> braids <global_val:pf_say_b>'s hair by the fire, badly, and neither of them minds.
<global_val:pf_say_a> and <global_val:pf_say_b> sit with their knees touching, watching the fire, not talking.
<global_val:pf_say_a> brings up something from a while back, and smiles a little.
<global_val:pf_say_a> starts a story with "Remember when…", and half the fire groans, because they do.
<global_val:pf_say_a> laughs out of nowhere at something that happened weeks ago, and has to explain it.
<global_val:pf_say_a> brings up an old day on the road, and for once it sounds almost funny.
